name: Primary Immunodeficiency with Predisposition to Severe Viral Infection
aliases: Severe Viral Infection Predisposing Primary Immunodeficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ESID Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Immunodeficiencies

criteria.description: Recurrent or severe viral infections requiring hospitalization or intravenous antiviral therapy
Laboratory evidence of impaired antiviral immune response such as decreased type I interferon production or NK cell dysfunction
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes known to cause susceptibility to severe viral infections
Family history of severe viral infections or known primary immunodeficiency
Exclusion of secondary immunodeficiency causes such as HIV infection or immunosuppressive therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent severe viral infections plus immunological abnormalities with exclusion of secondary causes; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to identify specific molecular defects when possible.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe respiratory viral infections requiring hospitalization
searchTerms: serious viral lung infections needing hospital
hospitalized for bad viral lung illness
chronic viral infections of skin and mucous membranes
long-lasting viral mouth and skin infections

common.symptomName: Persistent viral shedding beyond expected duration

searchTerms: low lymphocyte counts affecting T cells
failure to gain weight as baby

occasional.symptomName: Neurological complications secondary to viral encephalitis

rare.symptomName: End-organ damage from chronic viral infections
rare.notes: May affect lungs, liver, or CNS
searchTerms: organ damage from long-term viral infections
end-organ injury due to persistent viruses

laboratory: Lymphopenia with T cell subset abnormalities
Prolonged viral shedding on PCR testing
imaging: MRI brain abnormalities in viral encephalitis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as IFNAR1, STAT1, IRF7, or UNC93B1
other: Family history of severe viral infections
Poor response to standard antiviral therapies

distinguishingFeatures: Profound T and B cell deficiency
Early onset with severe bacterial and fungal infections
Absent or very low lymphocyte counts
History of risk factors for HIV exposure

redFlags: Recurrent life-threatening viral infections in infancy
Poor or absent response to antiviral treatments
Family history of unexplained severe viral illnesses or early death
references: Picard C, et al. Primary Immunodeficiencies with Predisposition to Severe Viral Infections. J Clin Immunol. 2020;40(5):678-689.
ESID Registry Working Definitions for PID Diagnosis. European Society for Immunodeficiencies. 2023.
